notes: Two DB performance fixes following the ThreadingHTTPServer upgrade. (1) _init_db() ran its full CREATE TABLE/migration/legacy-migration script on every single call -- effectively every request -- instead of once at startup; now guarded by a flag so it runs exactly once per process, and the enrich_cache purge is rate-limited to once/hour instead of every call. (2) /api/sync-status parsed the FULL multi-megabyte result_json blob for every configured account just to read metadata columns that were already stored separately; new _load_all_accounts_meta() reads only those columns, no JSON parsing. IMPORTANT FINDING: after both fixes, a direct comparison showed the same query still takes ~1.6s against the live DB file but ~0.02s (80x faster) against an identical copy on local disk -- because this project's folder is Google Drive-synced, and SQLite's WAL-mode small reads/writes/fsyncs are intercepted by the Drive sync client on every operation. This affects all database access, not just sync-status, and is a filesystem-location issue rather than something fixable in the query layer -- flagged for the user to decide whether to move aiq_cache.db off the synced path.
